Mara").[[35]](#cite_note-35) Jack Mara had died in 1965, leaving his share of the club to his son Tim. Wellington and Tim's personal styles and their visions for the club clashed, and eventually they stopped talking to each other. [NFL Commissioner](/wiki/NFL_Commissioner "NFL Commissioner") [Pete Rozelle](/wiki/Pete_Rozelle "Pete Rozelle") intervened and recommended a neutral general manager, [George Young](/wiki/George_Young_(American_football_executive) "George Young (American football executive)"), allowing the club to operate more smoothly. The feud became moot on February 20, 1991, when Tim Mara sold his shares in the club to [Preston Robert Tisch](/wiki/Preston_Robert_Tisch "Preston Robert Tisch").

In [1979](/wiki/1979_NFL_season "1979 NFL season"), the Giants began the steps that would, in time, return them to the pinnacle of the NFL. The **Beagle** is a British [breed](/wiki/List_of_dog_breeds "List of dog breeds") of [scent hound](/wiki/Scent_hound "Scent hound"), similar in appearance to the much larger [foxhound](/wiki/Foxhound "Foxhound"). It was bred primarily for [hunting](/wiki/Tracking_(hunting) "Tracking (hunting)") rabbit or [hare](/wiki/Hare "Hare"), known as [beagling](/wiki/Beagling "Beagling"). Its sense of smell and tracking instincts make it suitable for use as a [detection dog](/wiki/Detection_dog "Detection dog") for prohibited agricultural imports and foodstuffs in [quarantine](/wiki/Quarantine "Quarantine"). It is commonly kept as a [companion dog](/wiki/Companion_dog "Companion dog").

British Shorthair :: Health :: chunk_0008
A UK study looking at veterinary records found a life expectancy of 9.58 years for the British Shorthair and British Longhair compared to 11.74 years overall.[[23]](#cite_note-23) Swedish insurance data puts the median lifespan of the breed at >12.5 years. 82% of British Shorthairs lived to 10 years or more, and 54% lived to 12.5 years or more.[[24]](#cite_note-24)

[Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy](/wiki/Hypertrophic_cardiomyopathy "Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy") (HCM) can be a problem in the breed. A Danish prevalence study with more than 329 cats showed that 20.4% of males and 2.1% of the females had HCM, with an additional 6.4% of males and 3.5% of females judged to be equivocal.[[25]](#cite_note-doi10.1111/j.1939-1676.2011.0751.x-25) HCM testing of males used for breeding is now mandatory for breeders organised under the Danish [FIFe](/wiki/FIFe "FIFe") member, Felis Danica.[[26]](#cite_note-26)

The breed is thought to be at high risk of [polycystic kidney disease](/wiki/Polycystic_kidney_disease "Polycystic kidney disease") (PKD).[[27]](#cite_note-27)

A study of over 190,000 patient records in England found the British Shorthair to be less than half as likely to acquire [diabetes mellitus](/wiki/Diabetes_mellitus "Diabetes mellitus") as either [moggies](/wiki/Moggy "Moggy") or the overall cat population; 0.24% of British Shorthairs were diagnosed with the condition compared to 0.58% for both non-pedigree cats and the overall prevalence.[[28]](#cite_note-28)

In 2022, the British Shorthair was one of eight cats featured on a [series of UK postage stamps](/wiki/Great_Britain_commemorative_stamps_2020%E2%80%932029#2022 "Great Britain commemorative stamps 2020–2029") issued by the [Royal Mail](/wiki/Royal_Mail "Royal Mail").[[29]](#cite_note-29)

Macron formally became president on 14 May.[[167]](#cite_note-169) At 39, he became the youngest president in French history and the youngest French head of state since [Napoleon](/wiki/Napoleon "Napoleon").[[168]](#cite_note-170)[[169]](#cite_note-Napoleon-171) He is also the first president of France born after the establishment of the [Fifth Republic](/wiki/French_Fifth_Republic "French Fifth Republic") in 1958.

He appointed [Patrick Strzoda](/wiki/Patrick_Strzoda "Patrick Strzoda") as his chief of staff[[170]](#cite_note-france3grammontstrzoda-172) and [Ismaël Emelien](/wiki/Isma%C3%ABl_Emelien "Ismaël Emelien") as his special advisor for strategy, communication and speeches.[[171]](#cite_note-bfmtvleparcours-173) On 15 May, he appointed [Édouard Philippe](/wiki/%C3%89douard_Philippe "Édouard Philippe") of [the Republicans](/wiki/The_Republicans_(France) "The Republicans (France)") as [Prime Minister](/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_France "Prime Minister of France").[[172]](#cite_note-174)[[173]](#cite_note-175) On the same day, he made his first official foreign visit, meeting in Berlin with Angela Merkel, the [Chancellor of Germany](/wiki/Chancellor_of_Germany "Chancellor of Germany"). The two leaders emphasised the importance of [France–Germany relations](/wiki/France%E2%80%93Germany_relations "France–Germany relations") to the European Union.[[174]](#cite_note-176) They agreed to draw up a "common road map" for Europe, insisting that neither was against changes to the [Treaties of the European Union](/wiki/Treaties_of_the_European_Union "Treaties of the European Union").[[175]](#cite_note-177)

The summit is first known to have been reached by humans in 1953.[[96]](#cite_note-la-104) Despite the effort poured into expeditions, only about 200 people had summited by 1987.[[96]](#cite_note-la-104) Everest remained a difficult climb for decades, even by professional climbers and large national expeditions, which were the norm until the commercial era began in the 1990s.[[97]](#cite_note-japtimes-105) As of December 2024, [The Himalayan Database](/wiki/The_Himalayan_Database "The Himalayan Database") recorded just under 13,000 total summits, by around 7,200 different people.[[98]](#cite_note-106)[[99]](#cite_note-107)[[100]](#cite_note-108)

Kenney created *The Mayor's Task Force to Combat the Opioid Epidemic in Philadelphia* in 2016. The committee concluded its work and presented a final proposal in May 2017.[[27]](#cite_note-27)

In June of that year, Kenney and U.S. Representative [Bob Brady](/wiki/Bob_Brady "Bob Brady") negotiated a deal with [Conrail](/wiki/Conrail "Conrail"), the company that owns abandoned train tracks in [Kensington](/wiki/Kensington,_Philadelphia "Kensington, Philadelphia") that became a well-known area for open-air heroin use, to clean up the property.[[28]](#cite_note-28)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f5/Philadelphia_Mayor_Jim_Kenney_%2825550370434%29.jpg/250px-Philadelphia_Mayor_Jim_Kenney_%2825550370434%29.jpg)](/wiki/File:Philadelphia_Mayor_Jim_Kenney_(25550370434).jpg)

Kenney at an urban national wildlife refuge event in 2016

Kenney has supported opening [supervised injection sites](/wiki/Supervised_injection_sites "Supervised injection sites") within the city. On January 23, 2018, Philadelphia's Public Health Commissioner, Dr. Thomas Farley, announced he wants the city to establish one or more in the city. He cited [Vancouver](/wiki/Vancouver "Vancouver"), stating overdose deaths have been reduced, as has the spread of diseases like HIV and hepatitis C.[[29]](#cite_note-29)

Other city officials differ. Philadelphia Police Commissioner [Richard Ross](/wiki/Richard_Ross_Jr. "Richard Ross Jr.") has publicly stated he is "totally adamant against" the idea, but has an open mind and a lot of questions. Kenney has also said he supports the recommendation. Pennsylvania Attorney General [Josh Shapiro](/wiki/Josh_Shapiro "Josh Shapiro") disagrees that the sites are an effective path to treatment and suggested changes would be needed in both state and federal laws in order for such sites to operate legally.[[30]](#cite_note-30)[[31]](#cite_note-31)

* Male: 76.5 (2024), 75.8 years (2023), 74.8 years (2022), 73.5 years (2021)[[146]](#cite_note-148)
* Female: 81.4 years (2024), 81.1 years (2023), 80.2 years (2022), 79.3 years (2021)[[147]](#cite_note-149)

Starting in 1998, life expectancy in the U.S. fell [behind that of other wealthy industrialized countries](/wiki/List_of_countries_by_life_expectancy "List of countries by life expectancy"), and Americans' "health disadvantage" gap has been increasing ever since.[[148]](#cite_note-150) Average U.S. life expectancy in the United States has actually declined in four of the years following 2014 (the year when average U.S. life expectancy reached 78.9 years, its historical peak).[[149]](#cite_note-151) These declines were m

The river originates from several tributaries in the eastern part of the [Tibetan Plateau](/wiki/Tibetan_Plateau "Tibetan Plateau"), two of which are commonly referred to as the "source." Traditionally, the Chinese government has recognized the source as the Tuotuo tributary at the base of a glacier lying on the west of [Geladandong](/wiki/Geladandong "Geladandong") Mountain in the [Tanggula Mountains](/wiki/Tanggula_Mountains "Tanggula Mountains"). This source is found at [33°25′44″N 91°10′57″E﻿ / ﻿33.42889°N 91.18250°E﻿ / 33.42889; 91.18250](https://geohack.toolforge.org/geohack.php?pagename=Yangtze&params=33_25_44_N_91_10_57_E_region:CN-QH) and while not the furthest source of the Yangtze, it is the highest source at 5,342 meters (17,526 ft) above sea level. The true source of the Yangtze, hydrologically the longest river distance from the sea, is at Jari Hill at the head of the [Dam Qu](/wiki/Dangqu "Dangqu") tributary, approximately 365 kilometers (227 mi) southeast of Geladandong.[[45]](#cite_note-Winchester-45) This source was only discovered in the late 20th century and lies in wetlands at [32°36′14″N 94°30′44″E﻿ / ﻿32.60389°N 94.51222°E﻿ / 32.60389; 94.51222](https://geohack.toolforge.org/geohack.php?pagename=Yangtze&params=32_36_14_N_94_30_44_E_region:CN-QH) and 5,170 meters (16,960 ft) above sea level just southeast of Chadan Township in [Zadoi County](/wiki/Zadoi_County "Zadoi County"), [Yushu Prefecture](/wiki/Yushu_Prefecture "Yushu Prefecture"), Qinghai.[[46]](#cite_note-46) As the historical spiritual source of the Yangtze, the Geladandong source is still commonly referred to as the source of the Yangtze since the discovery of the Jari Hill source.[[45]](#cite_note-Winchester-45)

In 1950, the NBA consolidated to 11 franchises, then in 1954–55 shrank to eight[[25]](#cite_note-25): the [New York Knicks](/wiki/New_York_Knicks "New York Knicks"), [Boston Celtics](/wiki/Boston_Celtics "Boston Celtics"), [Philadelphia Warriors](/wiki/Philadelphia_Warriors "Philadelphia Warriors"), [Minneapolis Lakers](/wiki/Minneapolis_Lakers "Minneapolis Lakers"), [Rochester Royals](/wiki/Rochester_Royals "Rochester Royals"), [Fort Wayne Pistons](/wiki/Fort_Wayne_Pistons "Fort Wayne Pistons"), [Milwaukee Hawks](/wiki/Milwaukee_Hawks "Milwaukee Hawks"), and [Syracuse Nationals](/wiki/Syracuse_Nationals "Syracuse Nationals"). All of these teams remain in the league today, albeit the latter six in new cities. During the contraction, the league's smaller-city franchises moved to larger cities. The Hawks shifted from the [Tri-Cities](/wiki/Quad_Cities "Quad Cities") to [Milwaukee](/wiki/Milwaukee "Milwaukee") in 1951, then to [St. Louis](/wiki/St._Louis "St. Louis") in 1955. In 1957, the Rochester Royals moved from [Rochester, New York](/wiki/Rochester,_New_York "Rochester, New York"), to [Cincinnati](/wiki/Cincinnati "Cincinnati") and the Pistons moved from [Fort Wayne, Indiana](/wiki/Fort_Wayne,_Indiana "Fort Wayne, Indiana"), to Detroit.[[26]](#cite_note-26)
